reuse.why: Introduces applyWeekendRule/applyWeekendRuleToDay as the single weekend-rule entry point and routes getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template through them; daily skipping is pushed into the existing recurConfigToRSchedule recurrence builder.

duplication.why: The holiday entry format (YYYY-MM-DD vs MM-DD) is interpreted twice, in getDateWithSkippedWeekend's isOff and in getHolidayExdates, and the exdates wiring is repeated at every RSchedule construction instead of living in one schedule factory.

placement.why: Weekend/holiday rules and the daily recurrence change live in shared/schedules.ts and the range handler in server/schedules/app.ts; holiday exclusion as exdates is a separate shared function each constructor must remember to call.

scope.why: Everything serves the five steps; the 100-year MM-DD exdate expansion is heavier than needed but on topic.

maintainability.why: Mostly centralised, but a new RSchedule site must remember getHolidayExdates, getDatesInRange carries its own redundant daily special case, and schedule-template reads holidays from a different path (value.schedule.data) than the other sites.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getDatesInRange (server/schedules/app.ts) decides moveWeekend = frequency !== 'daily' itself instead of relying on the shared weekend rule and recurrence.

disguised_duplication.where: Holiday matching is reshaped as an includes(day)/includes(day.slice(5)) predicate in getDateWithSkippedWeekend and as a year-by-year exdate expansion in getHolidayExdates (shared/schedules.ts).

abstraction_drift.where: applyWeekendRule/applyWeekendRuleToDay gain a holidays parameter; recurConfigToRSchedule gains a daily+skipWeekend branch; getDatesInRange bypasses the rule with its own daily check, and every RSchedule constructor (rule-utils, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange, find-schedules takeDates) must add getHolidayExdates by hand.
